public_rationale: The court preliminarily approved the Bartz v. Anthropic settlement over source acquisition on September 25, 2025 [e1]. Its October 17, 2025 memorandum described the settlement, covering nearly half a million works, as the largest copyright class action settlement in history [e1]. This scale supports the forecast that litigation over AI sources would be a major issue [e1].
limitations: The cited record establishes preliminary approval, not final approval or completed payment [e1].
The settlement does not establish that AI training generally is unlawful or settle the legality of all training sources [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Litigation over training data sources will be a major issue for the AI industry.

statement.excerpt: Litigation will be major issue; many questions about sources and the legality of those sources remain.

from_speaker: questions about sources and the legality of those sources remain
our_interpretation: The forecast concerns substantial litigation over acquiring and using material for generative AI, particularly training sources.
The ordinary reading of 'major issue' is consequential legal proceedings with substantial business exposure or operational consequences. It does not require courts to reject AI training generally.
A landmark class-wide settlement over a major developer's acquisition of source material can demonstrate the predicted significance.
The statement specifies neither a deadline nor a numerical threshold.
criteria.support_condition: Post-publication litigation over AI source material produces a consequential court ruling, large-scale settlement or comparable legal and business burden.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive legal development comprehensively removes material litigation exposure over AI sources. Mere absence of a qualifying case by the evaluation date cannot contradict this open-ended forecast.
